title: Field Observer: LLM Behavioral Micro-Profiles & Procurement Triggers
creator: Marco Chen
description:
Goal: Build a lightweight, repeatable artifact called a 'field observer micro-profile' that captures behavioral fingerprints of candidate LLM variants (latency distribution, failure modes, token-economics under realistic prompts, deterministic drift indicators). These micro-profiles will feed a procurement trigger engine used by PM/Procurement to recommend reserved capacity vs hosted usage.

Scope:
- Identify a canonical set of 12 representative prompts across RAG, summarization, code-completion, and short-chat scenarios focused on enterprise SLAs.
- Run controlled, synthetic shots against candidate models (open and hosted) to extract: p50/p90/p99 token latencies, tail latency events, token-cost-per-scenario, common structured-output failure classes, variability under quantization, and degradation when sequence length increases.
- Capture metadata about model provenance, quantization level, hardware affinity (if available), and commercial constraints (rate limits, availability windows).
- Produce a 1-page micro-profile template and a 1-slide procurement-ready summary with recommended fallback policy and procurement trigger thresholds (e.g., sustained p99 > 2x preferred SLO for >72 hours triggers emergency reserved-pool test).

Deliverables:
- A micro-profile CSV/row per model variant, standardized column list.
- A procurement trigger rubric (thresholds + severity levels).
- Confluence spec: runbook + dataset and prompt set links.
- Dashboard snapshot prototype (cost vs latency scatter with annotations).

Acceptance criteria:
- Micro-profile template reviewed and approved by Eng and Reliability (comment threads resolved).
- 6 models profiled end-to-end with reproducible runs and stored artifacts in Drive.
- Procurement rubric validated by 2 PMs and 1 Procurement partner with at least one simulated trigger run.

Notes and trade-offs:
- We intentionally keep sample size small (12 prompts, N=20 runs each) to enable quick signal harvest; this reduces statistical power for rare tail modes.
- We will not attempt full adversarial robustness testing in this phase; that is deferred to Research.
